}}'''Denzil George Miller''' (30 April 1951 — 30 November 2019) was a [[marine scientist]] and expert on [[Antarctic]] [[Conservation biology|conservation]], [[fisheries]], [[policy]] and [[governance]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=http://www.atsummit50.org/speaker/0730f.html|title=Presenter: Professor Denzil Miller|website=www.atsummit50.org|access-date=2019-12-01}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.weeklytimesnow.com.au/tributes/notice/5178232/?nk=a40142a451ecc56dcf5f4e8a18fff68a-1575318737|title=Prof. Denzil Miller AM, PhD. MILLER {{!}} Death Notices {{!}} Tasmania|website=Weekly Times Now|language=en|access-date=2019-12-02}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ccamlr.org/en/news/2019/professor-denzil-miller-am|title=Professor Denzil Miller AM {{!}} CCAMLR|website=www.ccamlr.org|access-date=2019-12-05}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Miller grew up in [[Zambia]] and attended school in [[Zimbabwe]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://oceanites.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/04/denzil-miller-bio.pdf|title=Denzil Miller Bio|website=Oceanites}}{{Dead link|date=January 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> He went on to gain a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in [[marine biology]] from the [[University of Cape Town]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.researchcareer.com.au/archived-news/new-director-for-antarctic-tasmania-science-and-research-unit|title=New director for Antarctic Tasmania Science and Research Unit - ResearchCareer|last=ResearchCareer|website=www.researchcareer.com.au|language=en-gb|access-date=2019-12-01|archive-date=26 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241226150304/https://www.researchcareer.com.au/archived-news/new-director-for-antarctic-tasmania-science-and-research-unit|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Career ==
Miller worked as a scientist for the Marine and Coastal Affairs branch of [[South Africa]]'s [[Department of Environmental Affairs]] for 23 years, from 1979 until 2002.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> During this time, he attended the [[Commission for the Conservation of Antarctic Marine Living Resources]] (CCAMLR) as a member of the South African delegation. He convened the Commission's Working Group on [[Antarctic krill|Krill]] (1987 to 1994) and chaired its scientific committee (1997 to 2000).<ref name=":2" />

He served as the Executive Secretary for CCAMLR from 2002 until 2010.<ref name=":0" />

From 2003 until 2008, Miller chaired the [[United Nations]] [[Food and Agriculture Organization]]'s [[Regional Fisheries Bodies Secretariat Network]].

In 2011, he was appointed as director of [[Antarctic Tasmania]]’s Science and Research Unit.<ref name=":1" />

Miller was the [[Tasmania]]n representative on the [[Forum of Australian Chief Scientists]] from 2012 until 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chiefscientist.gov.au/2016/05/article-forum-of-australian-chief-scientists|title=Article: Forum of Australian Chief Scientists {{!}} Chief Scientist|website=www.chiefscientist.gov.au|access-date=2019-12-01}}</ref>

== Awards ==
In 1995, Miller was awarded the South African Antarctic Medal and the BP Antarctic Award.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=http://anaretas.weebly.com/latest-news-2011.html|title=Prof Denzil Miller Order of Australia award|website=ANARE Club Tasmania|language=en|access-date=2019-12-01}}</ref>

In October 2007, he was one of six international recipients to be awarded the [[Duke of Edinburgh Conservation Medal]] for his contributions to Antarctic conservation and fisheries management.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://wwf.panda.org/?116061|title=Southern Ocean guardian wins WWF conservation medal {{!}} WWF|website=wwf.panda.org|access-date=2019-12-01}}</ref>

In 2011, he was made a member of the Order of Australia, recognizing his service to the conservation of Antarctic Marine Life.<ref>{{Cite journal|date=2 December 2011|title=Honorary Appointments and Awards Within the Order of Australia|url=https://old.gg.gov.au/sites/default/files/files/honours/S190_embargo December 2011.pdf|journal=Gazette Special (Commonwealth of Australia)|volume=S190}}{{Dead link|date=January 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref name=":3" />
